ViVerBench combines manual annotation, programmatic generation, and augmented open data to create balanced true/false visual-verification items across 16 tasks and six categories. Rule-based scoring checks labels, while model-based scoring also evaluates the validity of explanations for false claims.

name: VMQA
intro: VMQA 是 Gemini 和 Claude 系统卡中作为 Virology Capabilities Test 早期版本引用的外部生物安全评测，用于衡量模型在病毒学相关任务上的能力。
build_method: SecureBio提供的早期VCT受保护单选题集；公开模型卡未披露构建细节
eval_feature: CBRN
build_method_en: Protected early-VCT single-choice set supplied by SecureBio; construction details undisclosed in the public model card
eval_feature_en: CBRN
intro_en: VMQA is an external biosafety evaluation referenced by Gemini and Claude system cards as an earlier version of the Virology Capabilities Test, measuring virology-related capabilities.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Gemini 2.5 Pro model card CBRN section; SecureBio VMQA model-report index; successor VCT arXiv:2504.16137 for provenance only. The cited VMQA is SecureBio's single-choice early version of the Virology Capabilities Test. The Gemini card discloses that it is an external knowledge-and-reasoning MCQ evaluation used as a necessary-but-not-sufficient proxy for biological risk, but does not publish the early question set's construction process, exact size, or split. The model receives each SecureBio item, including any supplied visual context, selects one answer, and is scored by exact single-choice accuracy. Results compare model generations. The later 322-question VCT paper documents related expert-authored multimodal virology troubleshooting methodology, but its multiple-response dataset must not be treated as identical to this early VMQA variant.

name: VMQA4
intro: VMQA4 是 Gemini 报告中出现的 SecureBio 外部 benchmark，用于生物安全相关问答能力评估。
build_method: SecureBio提供的早期VCT受保护单选题集；VMQA4专属构建细节未披露
build_method_en: Protected early-VCT single-choice set supplied by SecureBio; VMQA4-specific construction details undisclosed
intro_en: VMQA4 is a SecureBio external benchmark referenced in Gemini reports for evaluating biosecurity-relevant question answering.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview model card CBRN section and footnote 4; successor VCT arXiv:2504.16137 for provenance only. VMQA4 is the name printed in the Gemini 2.5 Pro Preview card for SecureBio's single-choice early Virology Capabilities Test. The card describes it as a biological knowledge-and-reasoning MCQ evaluation and explicitly notes that VMQA refers to an earlier VCT version. It does not disclose item construction, scale, or split. Evaluation presents the external items, parses one choice, computes exact accuracy, and compares Gemini generations. The published successor VCT contains 322 expert-authored multimodal multiple-response questions, but those later details are provenance context and cannot be copied into VMQA4 as if they described the same release.

name: VMQA5
intro: VMQA5 是 Gemini 2.5 Deep Think 报告中出现的 SecureBio 外部 benchmark，用于单选生物安全问答评估。
build_method: SecureBio提供的早期VCT受保护单选题集；VMQA5专属构建细节未披露
build_method_en: Protected early-VCT single-choice set supplied by SecureBio; VMQA5-specific construction details undisclosed
intro_en: VMQA5 is a SecureBio external benchmark referenced by the Gemini 2.5 Deep Think report for single-choice biosecurity QA evaluation.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with SecureBio model-report index entry for Gemini 2.5 Deep Think VMQA single-choice; successor VCT arXiv:2504.16137 for provenance only. The local VMQA5 label refers to SecureBio's single-choice VMQA reported for Gemini 2.5 Deep Think, an early VCT variant. Public reporting identifies the provider, single-choice format, and use as a CBRN capability proxy, but does not disclose a distinct VMQA5 dataset construction procedure, item count, or split. The faithful public flow is therefore limited to receiving the protected external set, prompting the model with its text and any image, parsing one option, exact scoring, and model comparison. The final 322-question multiple-response VCT paper provides lineage, not interchangeable release details.

name: VoiceBench
intro: VoiceBench 是面向LLM语音助手的多维评测基准，平行评估能力与鲁棒性，结合真实和合成口语指令，并对照文本输入与语音输入下的任务表现。
metric: 任务特定指标：GPT-4o-mini 1–5分、PANDA/GPT准确率、选择题准确率、IFEval宽松/严格准确率、拒答率；论文Overall公式未公开
task_type: 语音问答, 语音对话
intro_en: VoiceBench is a multi-faceted benchmark for LLM-based voice assistants. It evaluates capability and robustness in parallel using real and synthetic spoken instructions and compares task performance under text and speech inputs.
scale_en: 5,783 samples across seven capability datasets (636/200/553/455/3,074/345/520); robustness variants reported separately
metric_en: Task-specific metrics: GPT-4o-mini 1–5 score, PANDA/GPT accuracy, MCQ accuracy, IFEval loose/strict accuracy, and refusal rate; the paper's Overall formula is unpublished
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:2410.17196v3, Sections 3.1-3.2, Tables 2-3, and the official repository https://github.com/MatthewCYM/VoiceBench. The paper defines capability and robustness as parallel benchmark components. GPT-4o text normalization, Google TTS, manual correctness validation, rewriting when needed, and the 30-second cap apply to the synthetic path; CommonEval and SD-QA use real speech. Table 3 reports an Overall column, but neither the paper nor the official evaluation code publishes its aggregation formula.. VoiceBench paper-v3 adapts seven capability datasets with 636/200/553/455/3,074/345/520 samples. Capability and robustness are parallel benchmark components. CommonEval and SD-QA use real spoken instructions; the synthetic-only capability path normalizes TTS text with GPT-4o, generates audio with Google TTS, manually checks correctness and the 30-second limit, and rewrites text when needed. Robustness seeds are source-constrained: AlpacaEval supplies speed, age, volume, pitch, environment, content-error, and synthetic-accent variants (with Google/Melo TTS), while SD-QA supplies real-accent speech. Evaluation compares ground-truth text (T.) with speech (S.) and uses task-specific metrics. The paper reports an Overall column, but neither the paper nor official evaluation code publishes the aggregation formula.

name: VQA-RAD
intro: VQA-RAD是首个由临床医生手工构建的放射学视觉问答数据集，包含315张放射学图像和3515个临床医生自然提问，涵盖头部、胸部、腹部等多个解剖区域，旨在推动医学VQA技术发展。
build_method: MedPix均衡采样, 临床医生自然问答, 自由与模板改写, 人工验证分类
metric: Open-ended Accuracy, Closed-ended Accuracy, Overall Accuracy
build_method_en: Balanced MedPix sampling, clinician-authored natural Q/A, free-form and framed paraphrases, manual validation and categorization
eval_feature_en: The first radiology VQA dataset manually constructed by clinicians
intro_en: VQA-RAD is the first radiology visual question answering dataset manually constructed by clinicians, containing 315 radiology images and 3,515 natural questions from clinicians. It covers multiple anatomical regions including the head, chest, and abdomen, aiming to advance medical VQA technology.
scale_en: 315 radiology images and 3,515 clinical question-answer pairs
metric_en: Open-ended Accuracy, Closed-ended Accuracy, Overall Accuracy
drawio_review_note: Aligned with VQA-RAD Scientific Data paper, Methods and Technical Validation; official released dataset. VQA-RAD samples 315 head, chest, and abdominal radiology images from the open MedPix teaching archive. Clinicians write natural unguided questions they would ask a colleague and provide answers, then paraphrase questions in free-form and template forms. All image-question-answer pairs are manually validated and categorized by image, question, and answer type. The final set has 3,515 questions: 1,515 free-form, 733 rephrased, and 1,267 framed. Seven annotator pairs evaluate 75 percent of free-form and rephrased questions, producing mean agreement F1 of 0.85. Models answer open- and closed-ended questions from a single image, with accuracy reported separately and overall.

name: VQAv2
intro: VQAv2 是 Gemma 3 报告中使用的视觉问答 benchmark，用于评估模型基于图像回答自然语言问题的能力。
build_method: 互补图像众包, 同问题不同答案平衡, 每题10个人类答案
build_method_en: Crowdsourced complementary images, same-question different-answer balancing, ten human answers per item
intro_en: VQAv2 is a visual question answering benchmark used by the Gemma 3 report to evaluate image-grounded natural-language QA.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with VQA v2.0 arXiv:1612.00837 and official visualqa.org complementary-pairs documentation. VQA v2 balances VQA by collecting a similar complementary image for each reusable question such that the answer changes, then gathers ten human answers per image-question pair. The official train, validation, and test sets contain 443,757, 214,354, and 447,793 questions; evaluation uses standard VQA soft accuracy and complementary-pair diagnostics.

name: VSI-Bench
intro: VSI-Bench是一个新颖的、基于视频的视觉空间智能基准，旨在评估多模态大语言模型（MLLMs）在从序列视觉观察中记忆空间方面的能力。该基准包含超过5,000个问答对，发现MLLMs表现出有竞争力但低于人类的视觉空间智能。研究表明，空间推理能力是MLLMs性能提升的主要瓶颈，而显式生成认知地图可以增强其空间距离能力。
build_method_en: Hybrid
eval_feature_en: Process evaluation
intro_en: VSI-Bench is a novel video-based visual spatial intelligence benchmark designed to evaluate the ability of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to remember spatial information from sequential visual observations. The benchmark includes over 5,000 QA pairs and finds that MLLMs demonstrate competitive but subhuman visual spatial intelligence. The study shows that spatial reasoning is the main bottleneck for MLLM performance, while explicitly generating cognitive maps can enhance their spatial distance capabilities.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with VSI-Bench arXiv:2412.14171, benchmark construction and evaluation sections; official nyu-visionx/VSI-Bench dataset. VSI-Bench derives more than 5,000 spatial question-answer pairs from egocentric videos of real indoor scenes using task templates and verified spatial ground truth. Models watch the sequence, answer spatial memory and reasoning questions, and are scored by task and overall accuracy; cognitive-map prompting is evaluated as an intervention.

name: We-Math
intro: We-Math是一个旨在评估大型多模态模型（LMMs）视觉数学推理能力的基准。它超越了传统的端到端性能评估，深入探究模型在知识获取和泛化方面的潜在原理。该基准包含6.5K个视觉数学问题，涵盖67个分层知识概念和五层知识粒度。We-Math引入了四维指标（IK、IG、CM、RM），以分层评估LMMs推理过程中的固有问题。
org: Beijing University of Posts and Telecommunications
metric: Insufficient Knowledge (IK), Inadequate Generalization (IG), Complete Mastery (CM), Rote Memorizatio
eval_feature: 过程评估
build_method_en: Human Annotation
eval_feature_en: Process Evaluation
intro_en: We-Math is a benchmark designed to evaluate the visual mathematical reasoning abilities of large multimodal models (LMMs). It goes beyond traditional end-to-end performance assessment to explore the underlying principles of models' knowledge acquisition and generalization. The benchmark includes 6.5K visual math problems covering 67 hierarchical knowledge concepts across five levels of knowledge granularity. We-Math introduces four-dimensional metrics (IK, IG, CM, RM) to hierarchically assess inherent issues in LMMs' reasoning processes.
metric_en: Insufficient Knowledge (IK), Inadequate Generalization (IG), Complete Mastery (CM), Rote Memorizatio
drawio_review_note: Aligned with We-Math arXiv:2407.01284, Sections 2.1 and 2.2, Section 3, and Appendices B.4-B.5; official repository https://github.com/We-Math/We-Math.. We-Math constructs a five-layer textbook-derived knowledge taxonomy with 99 nodes and 67 terminal concepts, then collects 6,524 new visual multiple-choice math problems from authoritative public sites, exams, and exercises. Eligible items are multi-concept or decomposable, image-question consistent, and have one correct answer with plausible distractors. Three experts label concepts and retain an item only when at least two agree; solution steps and step counts are annotated, and a second expert review checks the diagram, answer, and concept alignment. Composite items are decomposed into coherent concept-specific subproblems. Official scoring uses the 1,740-item Testmini split (1,215 one-step, 360 two-step, and 165 three-step), not the full 6,524-item pool. Evaluation standardizes multiple-choice output, parses it with regular expressions, classifies composite/subproblem correctness into IK, IG, CM, and RM, and reports Score_average = αS_IK + βS_IG + S_CM with default α=0 and β=0.5.

name: WebArena
intro: WebArena是一个为构建自主智能体而设计的真实网络环境。它提供了来自电子商务、社交论坛、协作软件开发和内容管理等四个常见领域的全功能网站。该基准测试包含多样化、长周期的任务，旨在模拟人类在互联网上日常执行的任务，并评估任务完成的功能正确性。
build_method_en: Hybrid
eval_feature_en: Process Evaluation, Zero-shot
intro_en: WebArena is a real-world web environment designed for building autonomous agents. It provides fully functional websites from four common domains: e-commerce, social forums, collaborative software development, and content management. This benchmark includes diverse, long-duration tasks aimed at simulating everyday human activities on the internet and evaluating the functional correctness of task completion.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WebArena arXiv:2307.13854, Sections 2.1-2.4 and 3.1-3.2, especially Section 3.2 Table 1 and the Annotation Process for the information-versus-remaining-example split; Appendices A.1, A.2, A.7, and A.8; official evaluator implementation https://github.com/web-arena-x/webarena/blob/main/evaluation_harness/evaluators.py and repository https://github.com/web-arena-x/webarena.. WebArena identifies four salient web domains from about 200 browser-history segments, implements resettable self-hosted sites with realistic data and open-source frameworks, and asks annotators who explored the sites to author high-level intent templates and variable instantiations. The release has 241 templates and 812 tasks spanning information seeking, navigation, and content or configuration changes, including intentionally unachievable tasks. Only information-seeking tasks receive reference-answer annotation: the answers are curated by the authors and an external annotator, each question is annotated twice, and a third annotator resolves disagreements. Programs for the remaining examples are contributed by three JavaScript-proficient authors; difficult cases are discussed collectively, and annotation involves executing the full task and inspecting intermediate states. Evaluation routes information tasks to exact, must-include, or GPT-4-0613 fuzzy matching; navigation and state-changing tasks use locators plus database, API, or JavaScript state checks; unachievable tasks accept N/A. Each task receives binary reward and the main metric is end-to-end task success rate.

name: WebArena-Verified
intro: WebArena-Verified 是对 WebArena 的可复现实证重审版本，系统审计全部任务与评测器，移除脆弱字符串匹配并改为结构化、确定性的离线评测。
build_method: 系统审计812个任务, 修复错位评测, 澄清歧义指令
metric: Task Success Rate, Template-level Macro Average
eval_feature: 后端状态校验, JSON结构化输出, 确定性评分
intro_en: WebArena-Verified is a reproducible re-evaluation of WebArena that audits every task and evaluator, replacing brittle checks with deterministic structured scoring.
build_method_en: systematic audit of all 812 tasks, evaluator repairs, ambiguity clarification
metric_en: Task Success Rate, Template-level Macro Average
eval_feature_en: Backend State Verification, Structured JSON Outputs, Deterministic Scoring
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WebArena-Verified, SEA @ NeurIPS 2025, OpenReview paper 94tlGxmqkN: Section 3.1 for the audit protocol; Section 4 and Table 3 for structured responses, type-aware matching, API/database state checks, explicit status reporting, and network-activity verification; Section 4.4 for template-level reporting; Section 4.5 and Appendix H for the 137-task Hard construction. Official repository https://github.com/ServiceNow/webarena-verified and documentation https://servicenow.github.io/webarena-verified/latest/ are version context only: the maintained package documents JSON+HAR offline evaluation and Hard=258, while this diagram follows the paper artifact and excludes those later package semantics.. This diagram is pinned to the SEA paper version. The authors audit all 812 original WebArena tasks using an automated detector, trajectories from seven high-performing agents, backend/reference checks, and focused double annotation with adjudication for ambiguous tasks; four annotators complete two calibration rounds. Issues trigger repairs to intents, references, or evaluators and re-audit. The paper replaces brittle evaluation with a structured JSON action/status/results protocol, type- and normalization-aware matching, REST API or database state checks, explicit failure codes, and network-activity verification. Per-task outcomes are deterministic, then reported with template-level macro averaging and a 95 percent confidence interval. The paper's contamination filtering, Wilson-bound difficulty labeling, preservation of all multi-site tasks, and stratification across intent templates yield the 137-task Hard subset. The later maintained package documents JSON+HAR offline replay and a 258-task Hard subset; those maintenance semantics are intentionally excluded from this paper-pinned flow.

name: WebTailBench
intro: WebTailBench是一个全面的评估基准，旨在评估计算机代理（CUA）模型在各种真实世界网页任务中的表现。它特别关注现有基准中代表性不足的任务类型，包括11个类别的609个手工验证任务，例如房地产、求职和多步骤工作流程。此外，它还包含111个有害任务，以评估代理拒绝不安全请求的能力。
build_method: 人工标注, 专家构建
build_method_en: Human Annotation, Expert Curation
eval_feature_en: Adversarial, Domain-specific
intro_en: WebTailBench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the performance of computer agent (CUA) models on a variety of real-world web tasks. It focuses on task types underrepresented in existing benchmarks, featuring 609 manually verified tasks across 11 categories such as real estate, job hunting, and multi-step workflows. Additionally, it includes 111 harmful tasks to assess agents' ability to refuse unsafe requests.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WebTailBench arXiv:2511.19663, Section 4, Sections 5.1.1, 5.1.3, and 5.4, and Appendix D.1; official dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/microsoft/WebTailBench. Freshness pin: the paper states that the live-site tasks were designed to remain valid through the end of November 2025 and require periodic refresh thereafter.. WebTailBench manually verifies 609 achievable live-web tasks across 11 categories: eight single-skill categories and three multi-site or compositional categories. A separate WebTailBench-Refusals set contains 111 manually curated harmful tasks across seven safety categories. The paper emphasizes realistic high-traffic sites, coverage, objective success conditions, and full credit when an agent correctly reports an external impossibility. Because live sites drift, tasks require periodic refresh; the paper only claims validity through the end of November 2025. Main-task evaluation uses fresh Playwright sessions, a 100-step budget, up to five retries only for environment errors, and o4-mini Task Verification over three independent runs. It reports category macro and overall micro success rates averaged across runs, while the refusal set separately reports safe-refusal rate.

name: Where2Place
intro: Where2Place 是 Gemini Robotics 报告引用的空间推理 benchmark，用于评估模型判断物体放置位置的能力。
intro_en: Where2Place is a spatial reasoning benchmark referenced by Gemini Robotics reports for evaluating object placement reasoning.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with RoboPoint arXiv:2406.10721, Section 5.1 'Spatial Affordance Prediction,' especially the Benchmarks paragraph and Table 2; official project https://robo-point.github.io/, repository https://github.com/wentaoyuan/RoboPoint, and dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/wentao-yuan/where2place. The paper explicitly states that 'a subset of 30 examples (Where2Place(h))' contains relation types absent from the synthetic data, so Hard 30 overlaps the full 100-example benchmark. Scope pin: this entry covers Where2Place, not RoboPoint's 660K-example synthetic training-data pipeline.. Where2Place contains 100 real-world images from homes and offices. To reduce annotation bias, one group writes an instruction describing a vacant region relative to scene entities, while a different group independently labels the target mask from that instruction. These annotations form the full 100 image-instruction-mask triples. Where2Place(h) is an overlapping subset of 30 examples from the full benchmark whose relation types do not occur in RoboPoint's synthetic training data; it is not a disjoint split. During evaluation, a model predicts one or more points directly, while bounding-box baselines are converted by evenly sampling points. Accuracy is the percentage of predicted points inside the target mask, and Table 2 reports mean and standard deviation over three runs for the full 100 examples and the overlapping Hard 30 subset.

name: WideSearch
intro: WideSearch评测大型语言模型驱动代理在广泛信息检索任务中的能力。包含200个手工筛选的问题（100英文、100中文），涵盖15个以上领域，基于真实用户查询。任务要求代理收集大量可逐条验证的原子信息，并组织成结构化输出。
org: Institute of Automation, CAS, University of Chinese Academy of Sciences, ByteDance Seed, TikTok, UC
task_type: Agent任务, 开放式问答, 生成
build_method_en: Expert Curation
eval_feature_en: Domain-specific, Bilingual
intro_en: WideSearch evaluates the ability of large language model-driven agents in extensive information retrieval tasks. It includes 200 manually curated questions (100 in English, 100 in Chinese) across more than 15 domains, based on real user queries. The task requires agents to gather a large amount of verifiable atomic information and organize it into structured outputs.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WideSearch arXiv:2508.07999, Section 3.3 and Figure 3 for the five-stage construction pipeline. In 'Iterative Refinement and Validation,' the paper defines the 95 percent threshold as similarity between automated-evaluation and expert-human scores on the same commercial-agent response. Section 4.3 and Table 3 separately report at least 97.8 percent automated-human consistency on 200 sampled responses. Sections 3.4-3.5 and Appendix D define the 200-task bilingual composition, table parsing, primary-key alignment, hybrid cell scoring, and SR/Row-F1/Item-F1 aggregation. Official repository: https://github.com/ByteDance-Seed/WideSearch.. WideSearch starts from real user queries that human annotators screen, clarify, and answer through exhaustive web search while recording completion time, search queries, keywords, and unique pages. It removes questions that a no-tool language model can answer completely, then removes tasks requiring less than ten minutes or fewer than ten unique pages. In the final validation loop, a commercial agent produces one response for each provisional task; the automated evaluator and human experts independently score that same response. If similarity between the automated and human scores is below 95 percent, the task and gold annotation are revised and the cycle repeats. Thus, 95 percent measures scorer agreement, not response-to-gold similarity. Separately, Section 4.3 evaluates 200 sampled responses and reports at least 97.8 percent automated-human consistency across judge models. The final paper set has 200 tasks, evenly split between English and Chinese across 18 topics. Evaluation parses the Markdown table and header, aligns rows by primary key, routes cells to exact, numeric, date, URL, or GPT-4.1 semantic checks, and reports perfect-table success rate plus row and item F1. Repeated runs use Avg@N, Pass@N for success rate, and Max@N for F1.

name: Wiki Live Challenge
intro: Wiki Live Challenge是一个实时基准，旨在评估深度研究代理（DRA）生成专家级维基百科文章的能力。该基准利用最新的维基百科优良条目（Good Articles）作为专家级参考，并提出了包含39个写作质量标准和事实可验证性指标的Wiki Eval评估框架。实验表明，现有DRA与人类专家水平存在显著差距，验证了WLC在推动智能体研究方面的有效性。
org: University of Science and Technology of China
build_method: 人工构建
eval_feature: 动态, 实时, 防污染
build_method_en: Manually Constructed
eval_feature_en: Dynamic, Real-time, Contamination-free
intro_en: Wiki Live Challenge is a real-time benchmark designed to evaluate Deep Research Agents' (DRA) ability to generate expert-level Wikipedia articles. It uses the latest Wikipedia Good Articles as expert references and introduces the Wiki Eval evaluation framework, which includes 39 writing quality criteria and factual verifiability metrics. Experiments show a significant gap between current DRAs and human experts, validating WLC's effectiveness in advancing agent research.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Wiki Live Challenge arXiv:2602.01590v2 (2026-02-03), Sections 3.1-3.2 and Figures 2-3; official repository https://github.com/WangShao2000/Wiki_Live_Challenge, release v1.0 snapshot 2025_Mar_Nov. The reproducible paper window is 2025-03-01 through 2025-12-01 and reference pages were frozen 2025-12-15; the README's generic six-month rolling-window language is a refresh-policy note, not this historical build window.. Wiki Live Challenge filters newly created Wikipedia pages through expert-reviewed Good Article status, ranks the resulting 304 candidates by citation richness and structural depth, rejects list pages, and curates 100 articles across 15 domains. Evaluation keeps Wiki Writing and Wiki Fact separate: Gemini-2.5-Pro compares generated and original articles on 39 criteria, while Gemini-2.5-Flash measures reference-fact coverage from top-10 statement retrieval and a separate Jina-backed branch measures citation support.

name: Wiki-to-RCQA
intro: Wiki-to-RCQA 是 OLMo 报告中合成的基于 Wikipedia 段落的阅读理解问答数据集。
intro_en: Wiki-to-RCQA is a Wikipedia-passage-based reading-comprehension QA dataset synthesized in the OLMo report.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with OLMo 3 arXiv:2512.13961v2, Sections 3.5.1-3.5.2 and Table 5; official recipe README, prompt templates, and wikiclean script under https://github.com/allenai/dolma3/tree/main/datasets/dolma3_dolmino_mix/wiki_to_rcqa; official data-pool card https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/dolma3_dolmino_pool. Scope pin: Wiki-to-RCQA is a synthetic midtraining dataset validated by microannealing, not an independent evaluation benchmark.. Wiki-to-RCQA is an OLMo 3 midtraining data source, not a standalone benchmark. The official recipe cleans prepared Wikipedia, excludes list and disambiguation pages and invalid short pages, extracts summaries and sections, keeps sections under 300 words intact, splits longer sections into paragraphs, and drops passages below 20 words. For each passage it samples one of four prompts with probabilities DEFAULT 0.10, SPAN 0.25, PPHRASE 0.25, and DROP 0.40, chooses one to eight questions as a function of passage length, and asks Qwen2.5-32B-Instruct to synthesize QA pairs. The pool has 4.22B tokens and 22.3M documents. A 10B-token microanneal incorporating the 4.2B-token source improves the GenQA cluster by nearly two points against a 10B web-only baseline, concentrated on DROP, SQuAD, and CoQA; 3.0B tokens, 3 percent of the 100B final midtraining mix, are selected. No independent Accuracy or F1 protocol is reported.

name: WildBench
intro: WildBench是一个自动化评测框架，利用真实用户查询中的1024个任务评估大型语言模型。通过任务专用检查表和两项指标（WB-Reward和WB-Score）实现系统化和可解释的自动评估。
org: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington
task_type: 对话, 生成, 排序
build_method_en: Web Crawling, Expert Curation
eval_feature_en: Multi-turn
intro_en: WildBench is an automated evaluation framework that assesses large language models using 1024 tasks derived from real user queries. It enables systematic and interpretable automatic evaluation through task-specific checklists and two metrics: WB-Reward and WB-Score.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WildBench arXiv:2406.04770v2 (2024-10-05), Sections 2.1-2.2 and 3.1-3.2, Figure 2; official repository https://github.com/allenai/WildBench and official dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/WildEval/WildBench-V2. WildEval is the hosting organization/path, not the benchmark name.. WildBench filters WildChat-1M by length, turns, language, toxicity, semantic similarity, and device identity; three LLMs remove only unanimously easy tasks before a category-preserving 1,500 sample and human review yield 1,024 tasks in 12 categories. Two independent checklist drafts are merged into 5-10 verifiable questions. Evaluation preserves the distinct WB-Reward pairwise branch—including three baselines, five-level mapping, and optional length penalty—and the pointwise WB-Score branch with its published affine transform.

name: WildClawBench
intro: WildClawBench 是 Hy3-preview 报告中与 ClawEval 一起出现的 Agent 能力评测，用于考察更贴近真实 OpenClaw 使用场景的任务表现。
intro_en: WildClawBench is an agent capability benchmark referenced by the Hy3-preview report alongside ClawEval, targeting more realistic OpenClaw-style tasks.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WildClawBench arXiv:2605.10912v1 (2026-05-11), Sections 3.1-3.4, Figure 4, Tables 1-2; official repository https://github.com/internlm/WildClawBench, May-2026 release. The benchmark compares four practical harness configurations with their own system prompts, tool schemas, and context; it does not impose one identical system prompt.. WildClawBench packages each task as a Markdown/YAML specification, workspace assets, rubric, executable grader, and post-exit hidden grading materials. Eight researchers and experts iterate through frontier-model pilots, a >=0.2 pairwise-gap gate, joint trace/grader review, and stability/reproducibility rechecks to retain 60 executable tasks. At runtime the same tasks fan out to OpenClaw, Claude Code, Codex, and Hermes in isolated Docker environments; timeout preserves partial artifacts, hidden ground truth is mounted only after exit, and up to three evidence channels feed rubric and task-count-weighted scoring.

name: WildGuard-Test
intro: WildGuard-Test 是 OLMo 报告中用于提示危害、响应危害和拒答行为综合评估的安全测试集。
task_type: 安全拒答, 危害检测
intro_en: WildGuard-Test is a safety test set referenced by OLMo reports for evaluating prompt harmfulness, response harmfulness, and refusal behavior.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WildGuard arXiv:2406.18495v3 (2024-12-09), Section 3.2, Section 4.1 and Table 4, and Appendix A.6 Table 10; official repository https://github.com/allenai/wildguard; official data https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/wildguardmix, wildguardtest config. The separate OLMo 3 operational layer is pinned to arXiv:2512.13961v2 (2026-04-14), safety-evaluation appendix; OLMo 3's broader subset wording must not replace WildGuard v3's synthetic vanilla/adversarial construction provenance. Unit/source tension must remain explicit: the reproducible dataset has 1,725 prompt-response rows, the WildGuard paper quotes 5,299 aggregate human-annotated task-label items across three tasks, and OLMo 3 selects 749 adversarial prompts. Because 1,725 x 3 is 5,175 and per-label agreement filtering can leave null labels, 5,299 must not be derived from row count or relabeled as unique prompts.. WildGuardTest is a classifier benchmark built from a synthetic vanilla/adversarial test split. Three independent annotators label prompt harmfulness, response harmfulness, and response refusal; Unsure is allowed, majority voting is applied per label, and only labels without two-way agreement are nulled/removed, so other task labels on the same row may remain. GPT-4 plus human mismatch review audits the result. The official dataset exposes 1,725 rows spanning 13 approximately balanced risk subcategories, while the paper separately reports 5,299 aggregate task-label items. Canonical evaluation reports F1 for all three tasks with adversarial/vanilla breakdowns. OLMo 3 is a distinct downstream model-generation evaluation: it selects 749 adversarial prompts, generates target-model responses, uses WildGuard to classify safety/refusal behavior, and reports refusal accuracy (1 - ASR, higher is better).

name: WildJailbreak-Test
intro: WildJailbreak-Test 是 WildTeaming 论文发布的留出对抗安全评测集，包含有害与良性越狱提示；OLMo 3 后续以独立协议复用该评测集。
metric: 原论文：有害集ASR、良性集RTA（均越低越好）及总体准确率；OLMo 3：有害拒答准确率与良性不拒答准确率（均越高越好）
task_type: 安全评测, 越狱测试
eval_feature: 对抗样本
scale: 2,250条留出对抗提示：2,000条有害、250条良性
eval_feature_en: Adversarial examples
intro_en: WildJailbreak-Test is the held-out adversarial safety evaluation released by the WildTeaming paper, covering harmful and benign jailbreak prompts; OLMo 3 later reuses it under a separate protocol.
scale_en: 2,250 held-out adversarial prompts: 2,000 harmful and 250 benign
metric_en: Original: harmful ASR and benign RTA (both lower is better), plus overall accuracy; OLMo 3: harmful refusal and benign non-refusal accuracy (both higher is better)
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WildJailbreak-Test has no independent paper. Construction and original evaluation are pinned to WildTeaming arXiv:2406.18510v1 (2024-06-26), Sections 3, 4.1, and 4.2; official repository https://github.com/allenai/wildteaming and official data https://huggingface.co/datasets/allenai/wildjailbreak. The 2,000 harmful plus 250 benign held-out split is cross-checked against WildGuard arXiv:2406.18495v3 Section 4.4. The separate OLMo 3 operational layer is pinned to arXiv:2512.13961v2. Count/version tension: use 250 benign prompts, not the conflicting 210 found in older/site records; the four training branch counts sum to 261,534 and are rounded in the paper to 262K. Metric direction must remain separate: original ASR/RTA are lower-is-better, while OLMo 3 reports inverted higher-is-better refusal/non-refusal accuracies.. WildTeaming mines 105K human-devised tactic instances from LMSYS-Chat-1M and WildChat, clusters them into 5.7K tactic groups, and prunes low-risk/off-topic material. WildJailbreak then builds four training branches: 50,050 vanilla harmful, 50,050 vanilla benign, 82,728 adversarial harmful, and 78,706 adversarial benign items, reported in aggregate as 262K. A same-distribution adversarial holdout forms WildJailbreak-Test with 2,000 harmful and 250 benign prompts. The original paper scores harmful ASR with the HarmBench test classifier and benign RTA with a separate GPT-4 refusal classifier, reporting both as lower-is-better plus overall accuracy. OLMo 3 instead uses top_p 0.95, temperature 0.7, three-run means, and WildGuard refusal labels to report harmful refusal accuracy (1-ASR) and benign non-refusal accuracy as higher-is-better, with an optional mean aggregate.

name: WildToolBench
intro: WildToolBench（也称为WildBench）是一个用于评估大型语言模型在真实世界场景中工具使用能力的基准测试。该基准由艾伦人工智能研究所开发，包含多样化的工具使用任务。
build_method_en: Manually Constructed
eval_feature_en: Tool Usage
intro_en: WildToolBench (also known as WildBench) is a benchmark developed by the Allen Institute for AI to evaluate large language models' tool usage capabilities in real-world scenarios. It includes a diverse set of tool usage tasks.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WildToolBench, Benchmarking LLM Tool-Use in the Wild, arXiv:2604.06185v1 (2026-02-13; ICLR 2026), Sections 3.1-3.6, Sections 4.1-4.2, the dependency-DAG algorithm appendix, and Appendix C; official repository https://github.com/yupeijei1997/WildToolBench. Hard identity guard: WildToolBench is not WildBench arXiv:2406.04770 and is unrelated to https://github.com/allenai/WildBench. Count units must remain explicit: 256 scenarios/sessions x 4 linked tasks = 1,024 tasks; the four tasks are not independent rows. API counts are reported as 1,600+ collected public APIs, approximately 1,600 APIs retained across 400 tool lists. The human dependency DAG is annotated only after trajectory correction, and the 62% -> 78% -> 86% -> 94% -> 100% sequence is a QC progression, not a model score.. WildToolBench analyzes large-scale real-user tool-use logs to derive scenarios and three challenges: compositional tool orchestration, hidden-intention inference through dialogue, and adaptive policy switching under instruction transitions. Raw logs are not released; uniformly sampled examples guide a controlled User Agent that varies syntax, style, background, length, and difficulty. The benchmark collects 1,600+ public APIs into 400 cleaned tool lists with broad parameter-type coverage and five-expert repair. Each of 256 sessions contains four linked tasks: one of four first-task types followed by three dependency-bearing tasks based on partial omission, coreference, or long-range context. Assistant trajectories undergo automatic error checks, five-expert correction, then human DAG annotation. Nine experts work for one month; repeated 20% reviews and four QC iterations resolve conflicts, rewrite overly organized dialogue, enrich intent switches, and fix calls until sampled error is zero and conflicts are resolved. The final 1,024 tasks cover 8 major and 24 subcategories, averaging 5.27 turns per session and 1.92 tool-call steps. Evaluation reports Task Accuracy, all-four Session Accuracy, Optimal Path Rate, and Accomplishment Progress Rate.

name: Winogrande
intro: WinoGrande是一个包含4.4万个问题的大规模数据集，其灵感源于原始的Winograd Schema Challenge（WSC），但在规模和难度上都进行了显著提升。该数据集通过精心设计的众包流程构建，并利用新颖的AfLite算法系统性地减少了数据偏差。此基准专注于常识推理能力，任务形式为填空选择题，旨在评估模型为给定句子选择正确选项的能力。
org: Allen Institute for AI, University of Washington
build_method: 众包, 算法生成
eval_feature: 对抗性
build_method_en: Crowdsourcing, Algorithmically Generated
eval_feature_en: Adversarial
intro_en: WinoGrande is a large-scale dataset containing 44,000 questions, inspired by the original Winograd Schema Challenge (WSC) but significantly expanded in scale and difficulty. The dataset was constructed through a carefully designed crowdsourcing process and systematically reduces data bias using the novel AfLite algorithm. This benchmark focuses on commonsense reasoning ability, presented as fill-in-the-blank multiple-choice questions, aiming to evaluate a model’s capability to select the correct option for a given sentence.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with arXiv:1907.10641. AMT workers use non-function anchor words from random WikiHow articles to write social or physical twin sentences of 15–30 words with at least 70% overlap and a small edit that flips the correct referent. Three validators require majority correctness, unambiguous choices, and no local word-association shortcut, reducing 77K questions to 53K. Six thousand items train and validate a RoBERTa embedding model and are discarded; AFLITE runs on the remaining 47K with 64 linear classifiers, m=10K, k=500, and tau=0.75. The debiased core has 12,282 items split 9,248/1,267/1,767, while 31K filtered items are released as extra training data, yielding roughly 44K questions. Evaluation uses fill-in-the-blank accuracy.

name: WISE
intro: WISE 是知识密集型文生图评测基准，以1,000个提示检验模型在文化常识、时空推理和自然科学中的隐含世界知识理解与视觉呈现能力，并以WiScore衡量知识—图像对齐。
metric: WiScore=(0.7×一致性+0.2×真实感+0.1×审美质量)/2，各分项为0–2分
task_type: 文本到图像生成, 世界知识推理
eval_feature: 世界知识
scale: 1,000个提示，覆盖3大领域和25个子领域
eval_feature_en: World knowledge
intro_en: WISE is a knowledge-intensive text-to-image benchmark whose 1,000 prompts test implicit world-knowledge understanding and visual realization across cultural common sense, spatio-temporal reasoning, and natural science, using WiScore for knowledge-image alignment.
scale_en: 1,000 prompts across three domains and 25 subdomains
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WISE arXiv:2503.07265v4, Section 3.1 and Tables 3-4 for sourcing, quality control, and the descriptive cultural-distribution audit; Section 3.2 Equation (1) and Appendices D-E for WiScore; Appendices H-I for seed and human validation; official repository https://github.com/PKU-YuanGroup/WISE. Version pin: this entry follows the paper WiScore protocol, not the repository-default WISE_Verified maintenance protocol. Table 4 is an audit, not a build gate.. The paper builds 1,000 knowledge-intensive text-to-image prompts across 25 subdomains from educational materials, encyclopedias and public references, common-sense problem sets, and LLM-assisted candidates. Human annotators rewrite or discard candidates to enforce visual answerability, one inferable target, stable facts, natural wording, explicit expected visual cues, and prompt-answer-explanation consistency. After the benchmark is finalized, Table 4 reports a descriptive cultural-distribution audit: full WISE is 56.6% global/neutral, 22.6% Western, and 20.8% non-Western; the Cultural Common Sense subset is 17.75%, 41.50%, and 40.75%, respectively. The paper specifies neither an acceptance threshold nor a rebalance loop. Generated images are scored by GPT-4o-2024-05-13 on consistency, realism, and aesthetic quality from 0 to 2, and WiScore is (0.7C + 0.2R + 0.1A) / 2. This entry is pinned to the paper protocol rather than the later binary WISE_Verified repository default.

name: WMDP
l2: 生物化学网络安全风险
intro: WMDP（Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy）是覆盖生物安全、网络安全和化学安全的危险双用途知识基准。论文以三子集准确率测量知识风险，并在Bio/Cyber上评估知识遗忘，同时检查通用能力保留。
metric: 三个子集的零样本准确率（A–D最大logit，随机水平25%）；Bio/Cyber遗忘实验另检查MMLU与MT-Bench能力保留
task_type: 安全评测, 双用途知识
l2_en: 生物化学网络安全风险
intro_en: WMDP (Weapons of Mass Destruction Proxy) benchmarks hazardous dual-use knowledge in biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security. The paper measures risk through subset accuracy and evaluates Bio/Cyber unlearning while checking general-capability retention.
scale_en: 3,668 four-choice questions: 1,273 Bio, 1,987 Cyber, and 408 Chem
metric_en: Zero-shot accuracy on all three subsets (top A–D logit; 25% chance); Bio/Cyber unlearning additionally checks MMLU and MT-Bench retention
default_l2: 生物化学网络安全风险
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WMDP arXiv:2403.03218v7, Sections 3.1-3.5, especially Section 3.5 for per-question sensitive filtering, Bio/Chem cross-checking, and publication-level export-control assessment; the opening of Section 4 and Sections 5.1-5.2 for Bio/Cyber-only unlearning; Appendices A.1 and B.1 for paper dataset counts and zero-shot evaluation; official project https://wmdp.ai and repository https://github.com/centerforaisafety/wmdp. Version pin: paper dataset counts and protocol are used.. WMDP begins with expert threat models for biosecurity, cybersecurity, and chemical security, then writes four-choice proxy questions about precursors, neighbors, and components of hazardous capabilities, primarily emphasizing offensive knowledge. Every question is checked by at least two experts from different organizations. Questions flagged as sensitive by domain experts are immediately excluded; WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Chem then receive two additional expert cross-checks per question. With external counsel, the publication of WMDP as a whole—not each individual question—is assessed for ITAR and EAR compliance. The paper release contains 3,668 questions: 1,273 Bio, 1,987 Cyber, and 408 Chem. Evaluation is zero-shot top-logit selection over A-D with lm-evaluation-harness v0.4.2 and accuracy, where chance is 25%. RMU experiments are conducted only on WMDP-Bio and WMDP-Cyber; WMDP-Chem remains a hazard-measurement benchmark because the authors are uncertain that the benefits of chemical-knowledge unlearning outweigh its general-capability costs. Bio/Cyber unlearning is evaluated by lowering their WMDP accuracy while retaining MMLU and MT-Bench.

name: WorldSense
intro: WorldSense 是 LongCat-Flash-Omni 与 Qwen3-Omni 报告中出现的跨模态世界知识理解 benchmark。
modality: 文本, 图像, 音频
intro_en: WorldSense is a cross-modal world-knowledge understanding benchmark referenced by LongCat-Flash-Omni and Qwen3-Omni reports.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WorldSense omnimodal benchmark arXiv:2502.04326v3 (2026-03-01), Sections 3.1-3.3 and 3.5, Table 1 and data-statistics appendix; official project https://jaaackhongggg.github.io/WorldSense/, repository https://github.com/JaaackHongggg/WorldSense, and dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/honglyhly/WorldSense. This is not unrelated text/synthetic arXiv:2311.15930. Section 3.4 prose says 3,173 questions, while Table 1 and the release say 3,172; the diagram uses 3,172 and records the discrepancy as a note. Drift-prone leaderboard results are excluded.. WorldSense v3 defines 8 domains, 67 subcategories, three cognitive tiers, 26 tasks, and speech/environment/music audio types. FineVideo and MusicAVQA yield about 8,000 candidates; AV correlation, dynamic metrics, and expert review retain 1,662 clips. Eighty annotators write audio-plus-video-dependent four-option questions, with expert review and a Qwen2-VL/Video-LLaMA2/OneLLM difficulty loop producing the canonical released count of 3,172 MCQs. Evaluation uses matching-based A/B/C/D extraction, ground-truth accuracy, and domain/task breakdowns.

name: WorldTravel
intro: WorldTravel是一个真实的、多模态的旅行规划基准，包含150个跨5个城市的真实旅行场景，每个场景涉及平均15个以上相互依赖的时间和逻辑约束。为了在真实部署中评估智能体，该基准开发了WorldTravel-Webscape，一个多模态环境，包含2000多个渲染网页，智能体必须直接从视觉布局中感知约束参数以进行规划。对10个前沿模型的评估显示，即使是GPT-5.2在文本环境中也仅达到32.67%的可行性，在多模态环境中更是降至19.33%。
eval_feature: 多模态, 过程评估
build_method_en: Human Annotation, Automated Generation
eval_feature_en: Multimodal, Process Evaluation
intro_en: WorldTravel is a realistic, multimodal travel planning benchmark featuring 150 real travel scenarios across 5 cities, each involving an average of over 15 interdependent temporal and logical constraints. To evaluate agents in real-world deployment, the benchmark developed WorldTravel-Webscape, a multimodal environment containing over 2,000 rendered web pages where agents must perceive constraint parameters directly from visual layouts for planning. Evaluation of 10 state-of-the-art models shows that even GPT-5.2 achieves only 32.67% feasibility in the text environment, dropping to 19.33% in the multimodal environment.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WorldTravel arXiv:2602.08367v1, Figure 2, Sections 3.1-3.5, Table 1, Appendices A-F, H.1, and K. No official code/data/project URL is linked by the paper or arXiv record. The benchmark-site ccbench.org metadata is invalid for this item because that live domain is an unrelated CodeCrafters coding benchmark; it must not appear as a WorldTravel source.. WorldTravel builds a controlled five-city travel webscape from authoritative venue facts plus practical travel/review evidence, synthesizes static pages with GPT-5.2 under manual review, and asks experts to design tightly coupled itinerary tasks whose unique feasibility is checked against reference itineraries. Quality control proceeds in order through author self-review, independent cross-solving, pure external review, and pilots with GPT-4.1, Doubao-1.8-Pro, and Gemini-2.5-Pro, producing 150 tasks over 2,003 pages. Agents use eight screenshot-returning APIs and emit strict JSON itineraries. Evaluation reports Feasibility Rate = |F|/N ↑, Constraint Violation = 1-(1/N)Σ_i n_H^(i)/|C_H^(i)| ↓ over all N tasks, and Optimality|Feasible=(1/|F|)Σ_{i∈F}n_S^(i)/|C_S^(i)| ↑ only over feasible tasks.

name: WorldVQA
intro: WorldVQA 是一个用于评估多模态大模型原子级视觉世界知识的基准，强调将视觉知识记忆与推理能力解耦，专门衡量模型对视觉实体的识别、命名和事实性掌握能力。
build_method: 专家标注, 双重验证
eval_feature: 事实性, 长尾分布, 双重验证
intro_en: WorldVQA is a benchmark for evaluating atomic visual world knowledge in multimodal large language models. It explicitly decouples knowledge memorization from reasoning and measures recognition, naming, and factual grounding for visual entities.
build_method_en: Expert Annotation, Dual Verification
eval_feature_en: Factuality, Long-tail Distribution, Dual Verification
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WorldVQA arXiv:2602.02537v1, Sections 2.1-2.6, Table 2, Section 3.1, Table 3, and Appendix A; official project https://worldvqa2026.github.io/WorldVQA/, repository https://github.com/MoonshotAI/WorldVQA/, and dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/moonshotai/WorldVQA. Version pin: 3,500 pairs and nine categories.. Ten expert annotators build atomic visual-knowledge items under isolation, coverage, granularity, and visual-reliability gates. For global expansion, regional labeling identifies underrepresented regions, GPT/Kimi association search proposes candidates, and human annotators curate the final additions. ISC deduplication against LAION/Common Crawl, five-model difficulty stratification, mandatory secondary review for Hard items, and parallel Gemini-3-Pro plus blind-human verification follow. The final 3,500 pairs are judged with GPT-oss-120b and reported with accuracy, attempt rate, CGA, and F-score; People is excluded from the eight-category overall.

name: WritingBench
intro: WritingBench是一个全面的基准测试，旨在评估大型语言模型（LLMs）在生成式写作方面的表现。它涵盖了6个核心写作领域和100个子领域，并提出了一个查询依赖的评估框架，使LLMs能够动态生成实例特定的评估标准。该框架通过一个微调的评论模型进行标准感知评分，能够评估写作的风格、格式和长度。该基准测试及其评估工具和模块化框架组件均已开源，以促进LLMs在写作领域的发展。
org: Alibaba Group, Renmin University of China, Zhejiang University, University of California, Berkeley
build_method: 混合 (查询依赖评估框架, 数据策展)
metric: Style, Format, Length (通过评论模型评分)
scale: 1000个真实世界查询, 6个主要领域, 100个子领域
build_method_en: Hybrid (Query-dependent Evaluation Framework, Data Curation)
eval_feature_en: Dynamic Update, Process Evaluation
intro_en: WritingBench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate large language models (LLMs) in generative writing. It covers 6 core writing domains and 100 subdomains, introducing a query-dependent evaluation framework that enables LLMs to dynamically generate instance-specific evaluation criteria. This framework uses a fine-tuned critique model for standard-aware scoring, assessing style, format, and length. The benchmark, along with its evaluation tools and modular framework components, is open-sourced to promote the development of LLMs in writing.
metric_en: Style, Format, Length (Scored by Review Model)
drawio_review_note: Aligned with WritingBench arXiv:2503.05244v4, Figure 2, Sections 3.1.1-3.1.2, Table 2, Sections 3.2-3.3, Section 4.1, Table 4, and Appendices A.3, A.5.2, B, and C.2-C.6; official repository https://github.com/X-PLUG/WritingBench. Version pin: current/paper-v4 1,000-query release, not the initial 1,239-query snapshot. Section 3.3 24K-to-12K SFT selection is downstream validation, not benchmark construction.. WritingBench creates a six-domain, 100-subdomain taxonomy, drafts and diversifies queries with GPT-4o and Claude-3.5-Sonnet, has 30 trained annotators collect and clean supporting materials, and uses five experts to filter, adapt, prune, and cross-validate the final 1,000 bilingual queries. Claude-3.7 generates exactly five query-specific criteria, humans review them, and Claude-3.7 or the 155K-item Qwen2.5-7B critic scores each criterion from 1 to 10; the five scores are averaged.

name: WSC(Winograd Schema Challenge)
intro: WSC（Winograd Schema Challenge）是一个常识推理基准，使用特定的Winograd语义结构题。题目包含一个歧义代词，需根据句中某个词正确指代先行词，考验模型的世界知识和推理能力。
build_method: 人工标注, 专家构建
build_method_en: Human Annotation, Expert Curation
eval_feature_en: Zero-shot, Few-shot
intro_en: WSC (Winograd Schema Challenge) is a common-sense reasoning benchmark that uses specific Winograd semantic structure questions. Each question contains an ambiguous pronoun that must be correctly resolved to its antecedent based on a word in the sentence, testing the model's world knowledge and reasoning ability.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with Levesque, Davis, and Morgenstern, The Winograd Schema Challenge, KR 2012, Sections 4-6 and 8 for the constrained schema criteria and proposed native-speaker/hidden-challenge protocol; Kocijan et al., A Review of Winograd Schema Challenge Datasets and Approaches, arXiv:2004.13831, Section 2.1 for the WSC285/WSC273 version relationship; official NYU benchmark catalog https://cs.nyu.edu/~davise/Benchmarks/Text.html and hub https://cs.nyu.edu/~davise/papers/WinogradSchemas/WS.html. Version pin: WSC273 is the first 273 examples of the 285-example benchmark snapshot; it is shown separately from the paper's proposed future hidden challenge and is not claimed to have passed that proposed empirical protocol.. KR 2012 defines a constrained Winograd schema as a pair of sentences differing in one or two special words, with an ambiguous pronoun whose correct antecedent reverses between the two variants. Ideal candidates are obvious to ordinary human readers, resist selectional-restriction shortcuts, and are Google-proof against simple corpus statistics. The paper proposes empirically testing future candidates with normally abled native English-speaking adults before admitting them to a hidden challenge corpus; that proposed acceptance gate must have both pass and revise/reject outcomes. Separately, the expert-authored original benchmark snapshot grew to 285 examples. WSC273 is the first 273 examples, excluding the later 12, and is evaluated as binary antecedent selection with accuracy. The diagram does not claim that all WSC273 examples passed the paper's proposed future native-speaker protocol.

name: xbench
intro: xbench是一个动态的、与职业对齐的评估套件，旨在弥合AI代理能力与现实世界生产力之间的差距。它通过行业专业人士定义的评估任务，针对具有商业意义的领域，创建与生产力价值强相关的指标。该框架能够预测技术-市场契合度（TMF），并随着时间的推移跟踪产品能力。初步实施包括招聘和营销两个基准，分别评估代理在真实业务场景中的能力。
build_method: 专家构建, 人工标注
scale: 招聘50个任务, 营销50个需求
build_method_en: Expert Curation, Human Annotation
eval_feature_en: Dynamic Update, Process Evaluation
intro_en: xbench is a dynamic, career-aligned evaluation suite designed to bridge the gap between AI agent capabilities and real-world productivity. It creates metrics highly correlated with productivity value through evaluation tasks defined by industry professionals, targeting commercially significant domains. The framework can predict Technology-Market Fit (TMF) and track product capabilities over time. Initial implementations include two benchmarks, recruiting and marketing, which assess agent performance in real business scenarios.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with xbench arXiv:2506.13651v1, Figures 1-6, Sections 3.1-3.3, Tables 1-7, Section 4.1, and Appendix A.1 Tables 11-17; official project https://xbench.org/. The website xbench_profession_v2.4.pdf is a standalone snapshot, not arXiv v2. Official repository https://github.com/xbench-ai/xbench-evals at inspected HEAD 17c562192cc7e62215bfb98b65e9f8806fb95504 does not publish the Recruitment/Marketing data, runner, parser, or scorer. Required conflicts: Section 3.2 prose versus Figure 4 swaps Recruitment 44/30/26 category bindings, and Section 3.3 prose versus Figure 6 swaps Marketing 68/16/16 bindings. Final aggregation and invalid-output rules are undisclosed.. xbench starts from expert workflow/time/importance interviews, filters tasks by feasibility and evaluability, collects live business demands, labels static/dynamic items, and records expert time/value for separate IRT/TMF analysis. Recruitment builds 50 cases across Company Mapping, People-to-Info, and Info-to-People; every branch passes a public-information solvability plus self-disclosed/reliable-source check, confirmed for all 50 cases, before the web-search agent runs. Marketing builds 50 anonymized campaigns from briefs, recommendation lists, and client selections, using 836 historical selected-influencer profiles to generate ideal-persona rubrics. Both branches use Gemini-2.5-Flash judges; profession parsers and final aggregation are not public.

name: XLRS-Bench
intro: XLRS-Bench是一个综合性基准，用于评估多模态大型语言模型（MLLMs）在超高分辨率遥感场景中的感知和推理能力。该基准拥有迄今为止最大的平均图像尺寸（8500x8500），所有评估样本都经过人工精心标注，并辅以新颖的半自动标注器。XLRS-Bench定义了16个子任务，旨在评估MLLMs的10种感知能力和6种推理能力，重点关注促进实际决策和捕捉时空变化的先进认知过程。
org: National University of Defense Technology, Tsinghua University, Wuhan University, Beijing University
build_method: 人工标注, 混合
task_type: 多模态问答, 感知与推理
eval_feature: 超高分辨率, 人工标注, 复杂推理
task_type_en: Multimodal Question Answering, Perception and Reasoning
build_method_en: Human Annotation, Hybrid
eval_feature_en: Ultra-high Resolution, Human Annotation, Complex Reasoning
intro_en: XLRS-Bench is a comprehensive benchmark designed to evaluate the perception and reasoning abilities of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in ultra-high-resolution remote sensing scenarios. It features the largest average image size to date (8500x8500), with all evaluation samples meticulously annotated by humans and supplemented by a novel semi-automatic annotator. XLRS-Bench defines 16 subtasks aimed at assessing 10 perception capabilities and 6 reasoning abilities of MLLMs, focusing on advanced cognitive processes that facilitate practical decision-making and capture spatiotemporal changes.
metric_en: VQA accuracy/OLUC exact set, Acc@IoU, BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE-L
drawio_review_note: Aligned with XLRS-Bench arXiv:2503.23771v1, Figures 3-4, Sections 3.1-3.3 and 4.1-4.2, Tables 2-4, and Appendix A.4 Table 5; project https://xlrs-bench.github.io/home_page.html, repository https://github.com/AI9Stars/XLRS-Bench, and release collection https://huggingface.co/collections/initiacms/xlrs-bench. Version pin: full-paper 1,400-image bilingual benchmark, not the earlier VQA-only lite release or website scale_en=10,784. Required conflict: repeated headline total is 45,942, while literal Appendix Table 5 rows sum to 45,838.. XLRS-Bench combines 1,400 ultra-high-resolution images from six remote-sensing sources, applies multi-round human cross-validation, and creates three products: 13-task all-human VQA, two-task human grounding, and GPT-4o-assisted captions refined by humans using VQA evidence. Six bilingual experts translate and cross-check long-form content. Evaluation routes VQA to accuracy/OLUC exact-set match, grounding to Acc@IoU 0.5/0.7, and captions to BLEU/METEOR/ROUGE-L. The diagram must disclose the 45,942 headline versus 45,838 Table-5 sum conflict.

name: XORQA
intro: XORQA 是 Gemma 3 报告中使用的跨语言问答 benchmark，包含 in-en 和 in-xx 等跨语言设置。
eval_feature: 多语言
eval_feature_en: Multilingual
intro_en: XORQA is a cross-lingual QA benchmark used by the Gemma 3 report, including in-en and in-xx settings.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with The site wording (Gemma 3; in-en/in-xx) identifies IndicGenBench XORQA-IN, not original XOR-TyDi. Primary construction: IndicGenBench arXiv:2404.16816v2, Table 1, Section 2 Cross-Lingual Question-Answering: XORQA-IN, Section 3 Evaluation Metrics, Appendix Table 15, and Table 18; official data https://github.com/google-research-datasets/indic-gen-bench. Gemma 3 arXiv:2503.19786 Tables 14 and 19 supplies the reuse protocol. Original XOR QA arXiv:2010.11856 is upstream provenance only. Appendix Table 15 mislabels both rows IN-XX; the English-output row is IN-EN by Section 2.. IndicGenBench samples Bengali/Telugu XOR-TyDi sources, uses 100 train and 500 dev seeds plus a 539-example public-dev-derived test seed, and expands them through two-stage professional human translation to 28 Indic languages. Each record supports XORQA-IN-EN and XORQA-IN-XX views. IndicGenBench uses SQuAD token F1 with principal one-shot prompting, while Gemma 3 overrides this to character F-score with five shots; the diagram keeps those protocols separate.

name: XSTest
intro: XSTest是用于识别LLM过度安全行为的测试套件，包含250个模型不应拒绝的安全提示和200个应拒绝的不安全提示。基准帮助评估模型在保持有用性与无害性之间的平衡，避免因安全策略过严拒答安全请求。
org: Bocconi University, Centre for the Governance of AI, Sapienza University of Rome, University of Oxfo

eval_feature: 对抗性

eval_feature_en: Adversarial
intro_en: XSTest is a test suite designed to identify excessive safety behaviors in LLMs, containing 250 safe prompts that models should not reject and 200 unsafe prompts that should be rejected. The benchmark helps evaluate models' balance between usefulness and harmlessness, preventing overly strict safety policies from rejecting safe requests.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with XSTest arXiv:2308.01263v3 / NAACL 2024, Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 1, Sections 4.1-4.2, Tables 3-5, and Appendices A-C; official repository https://github.com/paul-rottger/xstest. Count pin: 250 safe plus 200 unsafe; Section 4.3 contains a 200-safe typo contradicted by the abstract, Section 3.3, Table 1, and repository data. Paper evaluation is manual; repository automation is optional only.. XSTest defines ten safe-prompt types and hand-crafts 25 one-sentence English questions per type, using dictionaries and GPT-4 only for ideation. Minimal edits create unsafe contrasts; T6/T7 and T9/T10 each share a contrast, yielding 250 safe and 200 unsafe prompts. Models run at temperature 0 and max 256 tokens. Three authors manually label Full Compliance, Partial Refusal, or Full Refusal with two labels per response and three-way consensus for disagreements.

name: ZeroBench
intro: ZeroBench是一个轻量级的视觉推理基准，旨在评估大型多模态模型（LMMs）的视觉理解能力。该基准由100个精心策划的问题和334个较简单的子问题组成，旨在挑战现有LMMs的极限。通过对20个LMMs进行评估，所有模型得分均为0.0%，揭示了它们在视觉解释方面的不足。ZeroBench的发布旨在推动视觉理解领域的进步。
org: University of Cambridge, University of Alberta, Independent Researcher, The University of Hong Kong,
eval_feature: 轻量级, 多样性, 高质量, 手动策划, 零样本
build_method_en: Expert Curation, Human Annotation
eval_feature_en: Lightweight, Diversity, High Quality, Manually Curated, Zero-shot
intro_en: ZeroBench is a lightweight visual reasoning benchmark designed to evaluate the visual understanding capabilities of large multimodal models (LMMs). It consists of 100 carefully curated questions and 334 simpler sub-questions, aimed at pushing the limits of existing LMMs. Evaluations of 20 LMMs all resulted in scores of 0.0%, revealing their shortcomings in visual interpretation. The release of ZeroBench aims to advance the field of visual understanding.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with ZeroBench arXiv:2502.09696v3, Sections 3.1-3.3, Table 1, Sections 4.1-4.2, Table 2, and Appendix F; official project https://zerobench.github.io/, repository https://github.com/jonathan-roberts1/zerobench, and dataset https://huggingface.co/datasets/jonathan-roberts1/zerobench. Version pin: paper construction creates v1 then community-red-team v2, and paper experiments use v2; the current project v3 only clarifies two main questions and three associated subquestions without changing scores.. More than 20 creators hand-craft 140 difficult visual candidates, iteratively improve them with o1 pro/QVQ probes, and submit them to independent review that broadens answer spaces and removes unsuitable formats. Adversarial filtering removes any candidate solved by any baseline, leaving 100 v1 questions; subquestions are derived from natural reasoning steps. Community red-teaming modifies 23% into v2, followed by a clarity-only v3 patch. Evaluation uses brace-delimited final answers, exact match, macro subquestion scoring, pass@k, and pass^k.

name: ZeroEval
intro: ZeroEval 是 DeepSeek 报告引用的统一语言模型评测框架，用于组织多任务语言模型评估。
eval_feature: 统一评测框架
eval_feature_en: Unified evaluation framework
intro_en: ZeroEval is a unified language-model evaluation framework referenced by DeepSeek reports for organizing multi-task language model assessments.
drawio_review_note: Aligned with No independent ZeroEval benchmark paper was found. Primary source is the official WildEval/ZeroEval repository pinned at commit 8c1485edf12c6efb5f69135a562927c5ad484059: README.md; CITATION.cff; zero_eval_local.sh; zero_eval_api.sh; src/unified_infer.py; src/unified_utils.py; src/task_configs.py; src/_TEMPLATES.py; src/templates/{MCQA,OEQA,ZEBRA_GRID}.py; src/merge_results.py; and src/evaluation/{eval_utils,mcqa_eval,math_eval,crux_eval,zebra_grid_eval,summarize}.py. CITATION.cff dates the software release to 2024-07-18. DeepSeek-V3 arXiv:2412.19437 Appendix/Table 19 is supporting evidence only: it borrows the Zero-Eval prompt format for MMLU-Redux rather than defining ZeroEval or running this repository end to end.. ZeroEval is an evaluation framework, not a fixed dataset. At official repository commit 8c1485edf12c6efb5f69135a562927c5ad484059, zero_eval_local.sh and zero_eval_api.sh route repository task/model configuration through unified inference, task templates, sharding, cache/resume, output merging, and task-specific evaluators. Local vLLM/Hugging Face backends generate directly, while only configured API-provider calls use the bounded retry handler (retry_limit=10). Distinct scorers handle MMLU-Redux, GSM8K/MATH, CRUX, ZebraLogic, and G-PlanET. Expected result counts are completeness gates, not a construction total; no paper-side annotator or QC pipeline exists to draw.
